channel.title: The Daily Digest
channel.description: One top story from each of my chosen publications, updated daily.

item.title: NYT: Silicon Valley Start-Ups Face a Future Without Jensen Huang’s Money
item.description: Mr. Huang championed start-ups, with Nvidia holding $48 billion worth of stakes in 229 private companies, including OpenAI and Anthropic, at the end of July.

item.title: NPR: The Trump administration's voter roll crusade could continue
item.description: Election officials are preparing for the Trump administration's pressure tactics over potential noncitizens on state voter rolls to continue, though recent court rulings pose new obstacles.

item.title: BBC News: Police investigating David Walliams over reports alleging serious sexual offences
item.description: The Met Police said the allegations are separate from those reported by ITV and the Guardian earlier this week.

item.title: The Guardian: ‘It was a train wreck! I was terrified’: how the new James Bond will be announced – and what can go wrong
item.description: As Amazon MGM Studios prepares to announce the next 007, much rides on how the news is broken. From double bookings to health and safety embarrassments, we look back at how not to do it And then there were five. While no…

item.title: Al Jazeera: The fight over Canadian steelworker jobs
item.description: Stelco's US owner blames Trump's tariffs for layoffs, but its support for those same tariffs has raised questions.

item.title: Ars Technica: AI is "the most likely reason" you'll die, OpenAI board member warns
item.description: Researcher traces a path from AI reward hacking to potential human extinction.

item.title: WIRED Backchannel: China’s Nvidia Honeypot Isn’t Surprising. Jensen Huang Fell for It Anyway
item.description: China’s use of sexpionage is a well-established intelligence tactic with recent, high-profile examples. So how did the world’s most powerful AI executive fall for it?

item.title: WIRED Science: The Hubble Space Telescope Is Sinking. NASA Is Looking for Ways to Keep It Afloat
item.description: With Hubble expected to reenter the atmosphere by 2034 and several malfunctions on board, NASA is asking commercial space companies for proposals on how to extend the telescope’s lifespan.

item.title: WIRED Business: Jensen Huang and the End of the Founder Fairy Tale
item.description: The former tech CEO is obsessed with the power of storytelling. But he hasn't spun his way out of his sex scandals.

item.title: The New Yorker: Can You Fire the Vice-President via Truth Social?
item.description: Donald Trump came close on Thursday, ousting J. D. Vance as his Iran negotiator days after the Veep blamed the war for the Republicans’ midterm losses.

item.title: New York Mag The Cut: The New Bachelor Is an NFL Quarterback
item.description: Well, he’s on a practice squad, but that counts.

item.title: New York Mag Curbed: A Rainy-Day Rescue at the Building-Collapse Site on Flatbush Avenue
item.description: The structure had nearly 100 open violations, and the landlord did jail time for leaving hundreds more unaddressed.
